# Final review — 30 October 2026

The review supports retaining A5 and A6 as the primary candidates and A4 as the less secure third. No new defect was found in the central proof arguments inspected. The remaining questions concern interpretation, originality and philosophical significance. This is a further assessment by an AI system involved in developing the essays, not independent expert review.

## Scope and findings

Claude's completed review was read at repository commit `3db2bdc0e04aaed585357f9363ede9ab42ca8253`. Its final essay texts match the preceding substantive package, apart from insignificant trailing whitespace in A5 and A4. A6's formal delta audit reports no required repair and numerical agreement with the preceding checks. The report's optional wording proposals were assessed against the manuscript. The present pass adds the requested readability changes and the bounded corrections below. It does not repeat the full historical computation suite.

**A5: a defensible, restricted challenge to the holistic derivation.** The published text of Dorst 2019, §4.2 and the proof of Proposition 5 on p. 207, was re-read. The distinction the essay draws is real: order independence of rational status does not itself identify the content of every background belief state. Dorst's passage introduces one truth-value-indexed increment after reasoning at an individual world; the essay's separation of truth-directedness from marginal extensionality addresses that step. A stronger interpretation can take these marginal restrictions as part of the setup. The essay acknowledges that reading and asks for its defense; it should not be presented as refuting every Lockean account.

The proposed increment is therefore the strict marginal-value counterexample and its diagnosis, together with the stated optimizer and sufficient refinement results. Non-monotone guessing and selecting a core are already prior art. The existing acknowledgment of Good Guesses remains essential.

A missing close comparison was added. Skipper (2023, §3.2) discusses changes in guess rankings caused by refining alternatives outside the compared guesses; §4 offers a score satisfying his independence requirement. This anticipates the general representation concern. His restriction preserves the compatible answers for the compared guesses, whereas the essay's RI quantifies over every coarsening. The new paragraph makes this distinction and credits the earlier objection. The Holguín reference was also aligned with the issue number in the indexed journal-PDF header. No formal result changed.

**A6: technically stronger after the earlier restrictions.** The mapping to Value and Weak Value was rechecked against the published Deference Done Better, pp. 104–107, 118 and Appendix B. For a fixed question, KDT with a fixed tie order supplies a recommended strategy in every decision problem. Universal safety therefore supplies Weak Value; Value conversely covers that strategy. The earlier paper's equivalence supports the essay's claim. Its general characterization predates this work, so A6's contribution must remain the normality-specific boundary and the analysis of the specified conditional inquiry rules.

The finite proof chain and the stated question-availability restrictions are consistent. The removal of the unsupported continuous generalization remains warranted: the finite theorem is not a necessity theorem about the second weighing alone. The encroachment discussion is now a conditional consequence of a particular comparison of inquiry evaluations. This pass adds “finite” to the informal graded-model gloss, states the criterion in terms of different option rankings, and specifies a normal situation in the Bjorn comparison. These are clarifications of existing assumptions. Claude's reported numerical reruns were not repeated here; the numbers and examples did not change.

**A4: retain with a clear significance reservation.** The witness-profile identities and the fixed-context argument were inspected alongside Halpern's Actual Causality, especially pp. 84–85 and 90–91. Halpern already identifies the modified definition's late-preemption problem and the older definitions' blocked-track problem. A4's intended addition is the exact comparison across models under profile anonymity and the stated Pareto condition. It is not the first failure of normality to resolve counterexamples, nor a refutation of every normality ordering. The new explanatory prose makes these restrictions easier to follow without extending the claim.

The result's value depends on whether the restricted policy class is a useful baseline and whether its distinctions illuminate independently motivated modeling choices. A richer ordering or different event representation can escape it, as the essay acknowledges. The earlier Wysocki comparison was retained; a fresh full-text copy was not obtained in this pass. The Section 7 regularity-theory computations remain author-computed and were not rerun.

## Access and review limits

The published version of Good Guesses could not be accessed through the publisher or the author-linked route. The previously inspected July 2021 author draft remains the basis of the detailed comparison. A publisher PDF would allow the remaining version comparison. The current Wysocki publisher page supplies only a preview, and the previously used PDF URL failed in this pass; its earlier full-text review has not been relabeled as a new one.

No exhaustive originality claim follows from the targeted search, the source comparisons or the computations. The next reviewers should focus on A5's interpretation and surviving increment, A6's significance beyond existing deference theory, and A4's restricted policy class. No contest form was submitted.

## Primary references checked in this pass

- Dorst, Kevin. 2019. “Lockeans Maximize Expected Accuracy.” Mind 128 (509): 175–211. [Published article](https://doi.org/10.1093/mind/fzx028), §4.2 and p. 207; local full text.
- Skipper, Mattias. 2023. “Good Guesses as Accuracy-Specificity Tradeoffs.” Philosophical Studies 180: 2025–2050. [Published full text](https://doi.org/10.1007/s11098-022-01915-1), §§3.2–4.
- Dorst, Kevin, et al. 2021. “Deference Done Better.” Philosophical Perspectives 35: 99–150. [Published PDF](https://fitelson.org/ddb.pdf), Theorems 2.2 and 4.1 and Appendix B.
- Halpern, Joseph Y. 2016. Actual Causality. MIT Press. [Book](https://doi.org/10.7551/mitpress/10809.001.0001), relevant preemption and normality passages; local full text.
